newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee prices may have to rise further.
newsitem.headline: German coffee prices may have to rise further.

text.p: Retail coffee prices may rise again in Germany if world market prices stay high, the managing director of roaster Melitta Kaffee GmbH told a news conference on Wednesday.
Melitta's Hans-Guenther Hildl declined to make a price forecast, but said companies would act if necessary.
Current prices around 190-200 cents per lb for nearby futures compared with levels of 120-140 desired by roasters, he said.
"On top of that, physical differentials are sky-high," he said, quoting 85 cents over futures for Kenyans and 35 cents for Colombians, compared with normal levels of five cents.
Volatile market also worried roasters, with daily movements of up to 10 percent prompted by fund activities and announcements of strategy by producer countries.
"A lot of politics are involved in coffee at this time of year, ahead of the Brazilian winter, when crops can be damaged," Hildl said.
"Fundamentally, there are no reasons for the current price scenario as crops should be sufficient to satisfy demand."
German roasters were implementing ex-works price increases of 1.50-2.50 marks per 0.5 kilos, which they had announced in March, Hildl said.
That was because green coffee prices had risen by 80 percent since December and the dollar had climbed to 1.70 marks from 1.50.
The price rises had been slow to reach retail outlets because wholesalers had hoarded coffee at the old price.
Also, retailers were taking deliberate losses on their coffee sales to attract customers.
Hildl said average Melitta prices were at 8.49-8.99 marks per 0.5 kilos but this did not fully reflect the rise of 2.50 marks sought by the company.
However, Melitta was aware 10 marks was a psychological barrier for consumers, who so far had not responded negatively to higher prices.
